newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Britain extends hold on Cypriot in bases clash.
newsitem.headline: Britain extends hold on Cypriot in bases clash.

text.p: A British military court in Cyprus on Friday extended the custody of a Cypriot whose initial detention earlier this week sparked violent protests from furious relatives.
The court at the British base of Episkopi on the island's southern coast granted a five day extension to a remand order against Greek Cypriot Angelos Panaretos, 39.
His arrest on Monday caused an uproar at his native Trachoni, a Greek Cypriot village east of Episkopi which lies within the jurisdiction of the British bases.
Some 50 relatives stormed the military police compound on Monday where they managed to free two detainees arrested with Panaretos. The man himself was being held in a separate wing.

Britain has held two military bases in Cyprus since independence in 1960. It enjoys sovereign rights in both areas, which include a number of Greek Cypriot-populated villages, but locals are increasingly questioning the arrangement.
The incidents prompted a strong reprimand from Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides who said they could harm relations between Cyprus and Britain.
Panaretos, a father of five, is under investigation for building a restaurant without a building permission, using threatening behaviour and assault.
He is alleged to have headbutted the deputy chief of bases police and breaking his nose.
"They have no right to hold me. I am going with my head held high," Panaretos told television cameras on Friday as he was led away in handcuffs by Greek Cypriot policemen employed at the bases.
